name: Oman
summary: Muslim estates follow Ibadi Sharia rules under the Personal Status Law, with fixed shares. Courts generally honour a non-Muslim expatriate's will made under their home law, but judges have wide discretion. No source on trusts or foundations was found.
reserved_share: Muslims: fixed shares under the Personal Status Law (Royal Decree 32/97, reported by secondary guide); Ibadi rules bar inheritance between Muslims and non-Muslims.
foreign_law_note: Practitioners report that Omani courts generally honour wills made under a non-Muslim expatriate's home law and do not usually apply Sharia to non-Muslims, but judges have wide discretion and may distribute otherwise. Bank accounts, including joint ones, are frozen until distribution.
trust_note: No trust or private-foundation statute was found for Oman; both answers are provisional.
open_questions: Royal Decree 32/97 and the Civil Transactions Law conflict rule not retrieved.
Trusts and foundations in Oman not sourced.
Oman's own non-Muslim wills procedure (if any) not confirmed.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
